title: When the Kiln Goes Out
logline: A crew feeds a wood-fired kiln through an entire night, reading the wind and the colour of the flame, and only once the feeding stops and the fire dies down can the kiln cool enough to be opened.
human_question: If something keeps going only because it is being fed, what happens the moment the feeding stops?

situation.what_happens: A crew loads a kiln, lights it at dusk and then keeps it going all night. Nothing about the firing is automatic: fuel has to keep arriving, the wind has to be read and answered, and the flame's colour tells them whether the heat is where it needs to be. The work is continuous because the fire is not self-sustaining for a single hour. Near dawn the feeding stops, and the fire is allowed to go down. Only then, and only after hours of cooling, can the kiln be opened, and what is inside is whatever the night actually produced.
situation.who_is_involved: The potter or workshop owner whose money is in the load; the crew who take shifts through the night, sometimes family, sometimes paid hands; whoever supplies the fuel; and the buyers waiting on the finished work.
situation.what_is_at_stake: A whole load, which is weeks of shaping and drying, and the wages of a night. Some breakage is normal; a badly run firing can lose most of it. There is also the exhaustion and the real risk of working with fire through the night.
situation.how_it_unfolds: A firing runs on an exact clock that cannot be paused: load, light, feed, watch, stop, cool, open. Its tension is that nothing can be known until the end, and its ending is whatever comes out of the kiln — mostly whole, badly cracked, or somewhere between. The weather can also postpone the whole thing.

concept_merge.why_together: C083 supplies the vocabulary: the sources' summary does not offer one notion of cause but a set of distinct kinds of holding-up — supporting by having been there first, by arising alongside, by feeding, by still being present, and even by ceasing so that what comes next has room — and it ends by saying there is nothing that is not a support for something. C082 supplies two of those in detail: nutriment, where what continues does so only because something keeps arriving, and presence, support given simply by a thing still being there, together with Margaya's match and box, where two things help make one flame in different ways and neither would be enough alone. A night's firing is a process in which every one of these is visible as work rather than as illustration.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Together they separate two things a single word hides: what makes something happen and what keeps it happening. What becomes visible at the end is that the stopping is part of the process and not its failure — the pots could not be finished by more fire — while the sources' own limit is kept in view: in the texts, support by ceasing describes one moment of mind making room for the next, not a life lesson about letting go.

concept_links.why: The summary of the conditions is precisely a list of different ways one thing holds up another, including presence and the support given by ceasing so the next thing has room, and it closes by saying no phenomenon is without some supporting role; a firing makes those distinctions into physical work.

Nutriment is support by something that must keep arriving, and presence is support given by a thing still being there; Margaya's match and box show two conditions helping one result in different ways, which is why neither fuel nor skill nor weather is sufficient alone.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: A fire lasts only as long as it is fed, and when the feeding stops it dies down. The texts say a living body, too, keeps going only while food and weather keep supporting it.
what_must_be_real: The crew's real skill, fatigue and financial stake, and the real result of the firing, including the pots that crack. Nothing about the night may be shortened or re-lit for the camera.
position_hint: closing candidate: it is the group's own hand-off made watchable — what is held up by being fed ends when the feeding stops — and it ends on a result rather than on an explanation.
risks: Turning the firing into a neat metaphor narrated over other people's labour.
Borrowing the absence condition as 'letting go makes room for the new'; the source means one mind-moment ceasing so the next can arise, in strict sequence.
Treating presence as a warm idea about showing up for people; in the source it is a technical relation that also supports craving.
Filming a night shift in a way that puts a tired crew at greater risk.

Letting a lost load read as desert or as luck; the sources' kamma condition is technical and describes its results as inert and quiet, never as reward or punishment, and nothing in the film may suggest a crew's loss was earned.
drop_if: No overnight wood firing falls within the filming window.
The workshop has moved to gas or electric firing.
The crew cannot be filmed through a full night without getting in the way of the work.

connections.note: Weather that shapes a community's mood also decides whether a long firing can be attempted at all.
Both look at what a long shared effort leaves behind once it is over: a finished, imperfect result, or different feelings in the people who remember it.

selection.reason: Used by EPD-0086; the links were re-grounded so the film rests on nutriment and presence rather than on a loose reading of the absence condition.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
